approach: In crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, an item's second failure ends as `ItemEnd::Failed(Failure)` with `Failure { reason, cause: Option<Cause> }` and `Cause { key, at_once }`. A cause exists only on positive evidence that the failure is not a verdict on the item: (a) `athena_core::disk::StopCause::of(reason).is_environment()` on a run that ended `Failed` or with no outcome, or on a read Err with no job; (b) a typed `GhFailure` found by `downcast_ref` in the Err arm of `landing_from_report`. Two tiers: `at_once` causes (StopCause LowDisk, ProducerAuth, UsageLimit; gh status 401 or 429) stop the drain on the first item that fails twice, because they are account-wide or host-wide and a second item would only burn two more runs; the other causes (CheckTimeout, OtherEnvironment, gh 403, 5xx, transient status-less) stop only when an earlier different item holds the same key, because one slow check or one pull request's permission can be item-specific. Every other run, read or landing Err is per item: declined, running, interrupted, already closed, readings cap, verification does not hold, Rejected, TimedOut, Work-reason Failed, red or open CI. `Drain::finish` stops with `Stop::RepeatedFailure` only for a cause; a lone failure is passed over with a note naming the item and its reason. Operator-facing text that states the old rule is updated, and a test fails if the old wording returns.

decisions.choice: A no-outcome run or read Err is per item by default. It carries a cause only when `StopCause::of(text).is_environment()` holds. A `Failed` outcome is tested the same way. Rejected, TimedOut and Work-reason Failed never carry a cause. `Run`, `Read` and `RealSteps::run` get no new field.
decisions.reason: The Err sites are item-specific: run/mod.rs ~340 declined, ~348 running, ~356 interrupted, ~360 already closed; run/pin.rs ~150 readings cap; run/close.rs ~412 verification does not hold. `RealSteps::run` turns them all into `outcome: None` (drain.rs ~3530-3613), so equal masked texts across items would stop the batch falsely. Typed `BudgetShort` and `LowDisk` set `held` and never reach the Failed path. The producer's usage-limit and expired-login stops arrive as `Failed` with those reasons, and the same test catches them.

rejected.option: Treat every no-outcome Err as shared
rejected.why: Job-state bails would stop the batch after two items.

rejected.option: Add a typed JobStateError in athena-core

rejected.option: Add a `Run.shared` field set from a GhFailure downcast in RealSteps::run

decisions.choice: Landing: add `Landing::HostError { why, cause }`, returned only from the Err arm of `landing_from_report` when a new pure `host_cause(&anyhow::Error) -> Option<Cause>` finds a `GhFailure`. Status 401 or 429 gives an at_once cause. Status 403 or 500..=599 gives a two-item cause. Status None gives a two-item cause only when `transient_reason()` is Some. Keys are `host: github <status>` or `host: github <transient reason>`. Everything else (404, 405, 422, non-transient status-less, non-gh errors, and the whole Ok arm: red, green, none checks) stays `NotLanded(text)`. `LandStep::NotLanded` becomes `NotLanded { host_cause: Option<Cause> }`. `landing_from_report` becomes `pub`.
decisions.reason: Auth and rate limit concern the host for every item. 403 can be one pull request's permission, so it needs a second item. transport.rs 30-35 gives status None to any non-zero gh exit without an HTTP code, so only the typed transient classifier (transport.rs 87-106) counts. Red CI is a verdict on the item. The key comes from the typed status or reason, not from text holding a pull-request number, so per-item data cannot defeat matching. `pub` lets criteria 3 and 4 build landings with production code.

rejected.option: Treat every status-less GhFailure as shared
rejected.why: Too broad; it covers not-found and other per-item failures.
Two red-CI items give equal masked text and would stop the batch.
Changes the tuple variant at every constructor (drain.rs ~5188, tests/drain.rs ~246); a new variant leaves them valid.

decisions.choice: Two tiers of stop, answering critic finding 7. at_once: StopCause LowDisk, ProducerAuth, UsageLimit; gh 401, 429. Two-item: CheckTimeout, OtherEnvironment, gh 403, 5xx, transient. The two-item tier compares keys: for CheckTimeout the StopCause Debug text; for OtherEnvironment and landing causes the key from `failure_key(text, names)` or the typed status. `failure_key` lower-cases, splits on whitespace, trims edge punctuation (backtick, parentheses, quotes, comma, colon, full stop, semicolon) and a trailing `'s`, masks whole tokens equal to a name (item or job), job-id-shaped tokens and all-digit tokens, and joins with single spaces. An empty result is None and never matches.
decisions.reason: disk.rs ~412 documents `is_environment` as the stop that 'says nothing about the work'. For usage limit, expired login and low disk a second item cannot fare better, so the first double failure ends the run, as the old rule did, and costs 2 runs, not 4. A check timeout may be one slow change, and an OtherEnvironment text may carry per-item data, so those need a second item as corroboration; this costs up to 2 extra runs on a true shared cause and is recorded in Risks. Whole-token masking keeps item `a` from corrupting words. Wrapped ids are real: close.rs ~348 writes run `athena go {id}` again, which gives a token with a trailing backtick, so edge-punctuation trimming is needed (criterion 5).

rejected.option: Every environment cause needs two items
rejected.why: Spends 2 extra runs on a usage limit or expired login that is certain to hit every item (critic finding 7).

rejected.option: Every environment cause stops at once
rejected.why: A check timeout or a 403 on one pull request can be item-specific; a lone item would stop the batch again.

decisions.choice: In `Drain::finish`, the `ItemEnd::Failed(failure)` arm: with no cause, note `item X failed twice and is paused for this run: <reason>` and call `pass_over`. With an at_once cause, call `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, Some(item.job))` with a note naming the cause. With a two-item cause, in ONE `self.st()` section look for an entry of a different item with an equal key and push (item, key) to `State.failures`; after the lock drops, a match calls `set_stop` with a note naming both items, and no match passes over. No Steps method is called with the lock held.
decisions.reason: Two concurrent workers (`drain_concurrent`) cannot both miss each other. It behaves like Paused and Skipped, and no Report field is added, so the JSON and the display prefix `repeated failure: item X failed twice` are unchanged. The failed item stays in `report.queued` and is not tried again in this run.

risks.risk: A true shared cause is missed, so the batch pauses items one at a time (a gh outage during a run, a Failed run with a non-environment text, an OtherEnvironment text whose per-item data masking does not remove, a status-less non-transient gh failure).

risks.risk: The two-item tier (CheckTimeout, OtherEnvironment, gh 403, 5xx, transient) spends up to 2 extra runs on a true shared cause before it stops (4 runs where the old rule spent 2).
risks.mitigation: Accepted cost, recorded in Decision 3: these causes can be item-specific, and the at_once tier (usage limit, expired login, low disk, gh 401 and 429) stops on the first item. The test for criterion 3 checks both tiers separately.

risks.risk: Two unrelated verdicts with the same fixed sentence (critic reject, planning cap, 'checks failed after rebase') are taken as a shared cause.

demonstrations.observes: The log is `read a, run a, reread a, run a-retry, read b, run b, land b` (a rejected job is retried, so it is reread, drain.rs 1566-1572). `report.stop` is not `Stop::RepeatedFailure`, `failed_item` is None, `landed == 1`. a is in `report.queued`; its job lines name outcome `rejected` and reason `ended rejected`. A note contains `item a failed twice and is paused`.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the old unconditional `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, ..)` in `finish`, the log ends at `run a-retry`, `read b` is absent and the stop is RepeatedFailure.

demonstrations.method: For each real per-item text, one serial drain of a, b, c with `Stub.runs` scripted as `(None, text)` for the four runs of a and b, then c landing by default. Texts use the real format strings with each job's own name: `job {id} is already closed (rejected)` (run/mod.rs ~360), `job {id} has 12 readings, the most a job may have; close it and ask again` (pin.rs ~150), `job {id} was declined: ...` (~340), `job {id} is running` (~348), `job {id} was interrupted: its process died before it closed. ...` (~356), `job {id}'s verification does not hold for its candidate any more; ask again` (close.rs ~412). Controls: (i) both items end `(Some(Failed), "the producer did not complete: crashed")`, a Work reason; (ii) a StopCause::Work-shaped no-outcome text. Assert only stable facts: `read c`, `run c`, `land c` present and after both of b's runs; each of a and b has two `run` entries; notes; stop; queued.
demonstrations.observes: A no-outcome run gives `retry: false` and `read: true` (drain.rs 1564-1573), then `item.read = true` (1792) makes the second attempt a pre-read run (1417, 1442), so the expected log is `read a, run a, run a, read b, run b, run b, read c, run c, land c` (critic finding 8 corrected; the old `read a` before the second `run a` was wrong). For the Work control the log has `reread a`/`run a-retry` entries. `report.stop` is not `Stop::RepeatedFailure`, `failed_item` is None, `landed == 1`, a and b are in `report.queued`, and notes contain `item a failed twice and is paused` and `item b failed twice and is paused` with each reason.
demonstrations.fails_without: Classing every no-outcome Err as shared stops the run after b, so `read c` is missing and the stop is RepeatedFailure. The old rule stops at a.

demonstrations.method: Serial `drain::drain` over a, b, c. Run cases use `Stub.runs` = `(Some(Failed), reason)` for the four runs of a and b. AT ONCE (stop at a): (1) `format!("{}: success: API Error: 429 {{detail 1}}", athena_core::disk::USAGE_LIMIT)`; (2) the `athena_core::disk::LOW_DISK` text; (3) the `athena_core::disk::PRODUCER_AUTH` text; (4) landing `landing_from_report(Err(GhFailure { status_code: Some(401), .. }.into()))`; (5) status 429. TWO-ITEM (stop at b): (6) `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` plus text holding each item's job name (exercises masking); (7) `athena_core::disk::CHECK_TIMEOUT`; (8) landing status 503; (9) landing status 403; (10) status None with text `connection reset by peer` (transient). Landing cases script FOUR `Stub.landings` (a, a, b, b) with pull-request paths /7 and /8. Controls that must continue to c: a single OtherEnvironment failure for a only, then b lands (two-item tier does not stop on one item); landings from `landing_from_report(Err(anyhow!("pull request 7 not found")))`, from GhFailure status Some(404), from status None with text `gh: not found`, and from `Ok(PrReport { state Open, checks Some(Red) })`.
demonstrations.observes: AT ONCE cases: `report.stop == Stop::RepeatedFailure`, `failed_item == Some("a")`, the log has no `read b`, and no queued item after a starts. TWO-ITEM cases: `failed_item == Some("b")`, a note names a and b, the log has no `read c`. In all, `display::drain(&report)` contains `repeated failure: item <failed_item> failed twice`. Controls: the stop is not RepeatedFailure and the log has `read c`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the cause test a lone failure always passes over, so the stop cases run c and end with the queue empty. Under the old rule they stop at a, so the two-item cases' `failed_item == Some("b")` fails. Without the at_once tier the cases 1-5 run b and `failed_item` is b. Without the origin split and the status-less rule, the controls stop.

demonstrations.observes: `landing_from_report(Err(GhFailure{status Some(503)}.into()))` gives `Landing::HostError` with key `host: github 503` and `at_once == false`; with `.context("after 3 attempts")` the same key (the downcast sees through context). 401 and 429 give HostError with `at_once == true`; 403 gives HostError with `at_once == false`. Status None with `timeout` or `connection reset` text gives a two-item HostError (`host: github timeout`, `host: github connection reset`). Status None with `not logged in` or `not found`, status 404, 405, 422 and a plain `anyhow!` give `NotLanded`. Ok/Open/Red, Ok/Open/Green and Ok/Open/None give `NotLanded`; Ok/Open/Pending gives `Waiting`; Ok/Landed gives `Landed` (unchanged).
